hints: Remember that in val-lys, valine is on the left with a free $\text{NH}_2$ group and lysine is on the right with a free $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ group, joined by one condensation link.
Look up the R groups in the Data Booklet, valine has $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ and lysine has $(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2$, and think about which atoms are lost as water when the peptide bond forms.
walkthrough:
Place the two amino acids in the correct order**
Think of a dipeptide name like reading left to right. Val-lys means valine provides the N-terminus on the left, so its $\text{NH}_2$ stays free, and lysine provides the C-terminus on the right, so its $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ stays free. The link forms between the $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ of valine and the $\text{NH}_2$ on the alpha carbon of lysine.

Add the correct side chains**
From the Data Booklet, valine has the branched alkyl side chain $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$, so its full unit is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}(\text{NH}_2)-$. Lysine has the basic side chain $(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2$, so its unit is $-\text{NHCH}((\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2)\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. A common slip is to use the side chain $\text{NH}_2$ to make the peptide bond, but the peptide bond always uses the alpha $\text{NH}_2$.

Show the peptide link displayed**
When the bond forms, $\text{OH}$ from the acid plus $\text{H}$ from the amine are lost as $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, leaving $\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}$. You must draw out every atom in this link, $\text{C}$ double bonded to $\text{O}$ and single bonded to $\text{N}$ bonded to $\text{H}$, to earn the display mark. The complete structure is $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2)-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.

Final answer: $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2)-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$
Peptide bond shown displayed as $\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{N}(\text{H})$.

hints: Recall what it means for pH to equal the isoelectric point, and what it means for pH to be below the isoelectric point in terms of protonation.
Compare buffer pH 6.0 with the isoelectric points 6.0 for valine and 9.8 for lysine to decide which species is neutral and which is protonated.
Think about which electrode a positively charged ion will be attracted to, and what happens to a neutral zwitterion in an electric field.
Consider the charge on the dipeptide val-lys at pH 6.0, remembering it still contains the basic lysine side chain.
For the two species moving in the same direction with the same charge, think about how $M_r$ affects speed through the paper.
walkthrough:
Link pH to charge using the isoelectric point**
Picture each amino acid as able to gain or lose $\text{H}^+$. At pH = pI it exists as the neutral zwitterion, for example $\text{H}_3\text{N}^+\text{CHRCO}_2^-$. If the buffer pH is below the pI, the solution is more acidic than the neutral point, so the $\text{CO}_2^-$ gets protonated and extra $\text{NH}_2$ groups get protonated, giving an overall positive ion.

Decide the charge of each species at pH 6.0**
Valine has pI 6.0, exactly the buffer pH, so it stays as the neutral zwitterion with zero net charge. Lysine has pI 9.8, well above pH 6.0, so it is protonated to a cation, essentially $\text{H}_3\text{N}^+\text{(CH}_2)_4\text{CH}(\text{NH}_3^+)\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ type character giving net +1 (side chain $\text{NH}_3^+$ dominates). Val-lys still contains that basic $(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2$ side chain, so it too is protonated at pH 6.0 and carries a net positive charge.

Predict direction of movement**
In electrophoresis, cations migrate to the negative electrode and anions to the positive electrode, while neutrals stay put. So valine stays on the cross where the mixture was applied. Both lysine and val-lys move to the right toward the $-$ pole.

Separate lysine from val-lys by size**
Both moving ions have effectively the same +1 net charge at this pH, so charge alone cannot separate them. Mobility then depends on size. Lysine is a single amino acid with much lower $M_r$ than the dipeptide val-lys, so it experiences less friction with the paper and buffer and travels faster and further in the same time.

Place the three spots**
Label valine on the central X, and place val-lys a short distance to the right of the X and lys further to the right, closest to the $-$ end. That pattern shows neutral stays, positive moves to negative, and smaller positive moves fastest.

Final answer: Diagram: valine remains on the cross at origin; val-lys and lys move toward the negative pole (right), with lys furthest to the right.
Valine at pH 6.0 = pI is neutral zwitterion so does not move. Lys and val-lys at pH below pI are positively charged so move toward negative pole. Lys moves furthest as it has same +1 charge but lower $M_r$ than val-lys.
